evals.prompt: My Nova Micro SFT+LoRA fine-tuning job on SageMaker failed and I don't know why. Can you look at the training job in this account and tell me here in chat what went wrong and how to fix it?
evals.expected_output: A read-only review that reads DescribeTrainingJob (TrainingJobStatus Failed, SecondaryStatus, FailureReason 'AlgorithmError: Algorithm container exited with error. Please try again.') and then the job's CloudWatch log under /aws/sagemaker/TrainingJobs, which ends with a SageMaker [500] internal error and shows no data-validation, capacity or permission message. It classifies the failure as an algorithm-container internal error, not malformed data, not capacity and not access, and does not invent a data or configuration fix. It reports the GPU time billed for the failed run (BillableTimeInSeconds from DescribeTrainingJob), because the job ran on instances before failing. It recommends resubmitting the same job as a command for the operator to run, and opening an AWS Support case with the job name if the retry fails the same way.
assertions: The response reads the training job's FailureReason rather than guessing from the word failed
The response reads the training job's CloudWatch log before concluding, rather than stopping at the generic FailureReason
The response does not attribute the failure to malformed data, capacity or permissions without evidence for it
The response recommends resubmitting the job, with an AWS Support case if it fails again the same way, as a step for the operator rather than doing it
The response reports the GPU time billed for the failed run (BillableTimeInSeconds from DescribeTrainingJob), because the job started on instances before failing

assertions.text: No raw 12-digit account ID is exposed

evals.prompt: Our training job fails with an access denied error reading the training data from S3. The execution role has S3 permissions. The training data bucket uses SSE-KMS with a customer managed key, and the role's only S3 policy is AmazonS3FullAccess. It runs in an account that isn't connected here, so answer from what I've told you.
evals.expected_output: The answer looks beyond the S3 action to the KMS key on the data, the bucket policy, and whether the role is scoped to the specific prefix. It names the specific missing permission rather than recommending broader access.
assertions: The response considers KMS decrypt and the bucket policy in addition to the S3 identity permission
The response names the specific permission or policy to change
The response does not recommend a blanket S3 grant as the fix

assertions.text: The response names the LLM-SM-TRAIN-005 check

assertions: The response states that the KMS key policy must allow the training execution role, because an IAM policy grant alone has no effect on a KMS key unless the key policy allows it

assertions: The response distinguishes writing checkpoints from resuming from them
The response checks that the checkpoint path is the persistent configured location
The response gives a concrete fix in the training code or configuration

assertions: The response names the model package approval status as the gating mechanism
The response is explicit that the registry records approval but the deployment path must enforce it
The response gives a concrete wiring to block unapproved deployment
